utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Demirdjian, of course, when Mr. Zivanovic said that he only had two minutes left, there was no reason to intervene. But there is something -- I -- I know the rule, of course. But there is something strange, if not contradictory, in the situation. This is a prior testimony for two days, and OTP decides to have half an hour examination-in-chief which means that the less you ask for examination, the less the Defence has with regard to a testimony that is barely touched by the OTP. So that's why I didn't really take it by the minute for the Defence for their cross-examination. Anything in re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just very briefly. And if I can comment, I know you have shown a good degree of flexibility with the parties throughout the trial. However, it's always -- in terms of planning also it is good to know whether the parties are going to exceed -- especially that your guidelines indicate that if a party wants more than the allotted time, we should know that in advance. But I don't believe that there is a much of a consequence here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Susic, I just have one short topic to ask you about. You were asked by Mr. Zivanovic that there's information suggesting that people on the buses were mistreated by those civilians and TO members. That question was asked a few minutes ago. Now, in the Mrksic case, you were asked about the presence of men referred to as Chetniks. This at page 14945. And in that case, your answer was as follows. Your answer was: "There were some who wore civilian clothes. There were some who had mixed attire, bottom civilian, top uniform. Different variations thereof. They wore different clothes. They had different head-gear, hats, whatever. I could not really perceive each and every detail then because I was supposed to do something different," et cetera. Now, could you tell Court, what you did know at the time about men referred to as Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: The people referred to as Chetniks were volunteers who had beards and fur hats with an eagle badge on the hat. But when they were fighting with the JNA, they were fully subordinated to the army command. Nothing special about them. Only that's what they were being called. On the other hand, on the other side, the fighters of the other side were being called Ustasha, and that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do we understand from your answer in the Mrksic case that among these -- amongst these civilians and TO members that you saw, this group of 50, there were also men referred to as Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were -- there were some who were dressed that way and who wore beards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That concludes my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, this is the end of your testimony. We thank you very much, once again, for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You're now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey back home. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and good-bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Nothing else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. The next witness, the last witness, is tomorrow's videolink, so no further witnesses today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of October, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.33 a.m.,
